Explore Python snippet +
Rainfall_Data_Anaqalysis.py
def weighted_corr(frame: pd.DataFrame, x_col: str, y_col: str) -> float:
    valid = frame[[x_col, y_col]].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna()
    if len(valid) < 3:
        return float("nan")
    if valid[x_col].std(ddof=0) == 0 or valid[y_col].std(ddof=0) == 0:
        return float("nan")
    return float(valid[x_col].corr(valid[y_col]))

AI tools08

AI subtitle translator

A Django pipeline combining Whisper, neural translation and FFmpeg. Explore the SRT writer; generated videos are not committed in this revision.

Explore Python snippet +
srt_generator.py
def format_time(seconds):
    hrs = int(seconds // 3600)
    mins = int((seconds % 3600) // 60)
    secs = int(seconds % 60)
    millis = int((seconds - int(seconds)) * 1000)
    return f"{hrs:02}:{mins:02}:{secs:02},{millis:03}"

def create_srt(segments, output_path):
    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for i, seg in enumerate(segments, 1):
            start = format_time(seg["start"])
            end = format_time(seg["end"])
            text = seg["text"].strip()
            f.write(f"{i}\n{start} --> {end}\n{text}\n\n")

02 / THE PERSON BEHIND THE CODE

A scientist by profession.
An educator by practice.

I work as a Project Scientist I at the India Meteorological Department, where I analyse climate and environmental data and build the Python pipelines that turn it into forecasts and reports. Before that, I completed a Master of Science in Information Science at the University of Arizona and a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science from Cooch Behar Government Engineering College.

My teaching draws on practical work with rainfall data pipelines, machine learning and AI tools. Classes connect core concepts with real code: a first loop, an analysis workflow, model evaluation or a tool-calling agent.

Classes are one-to-one and built around what you're trying to get to: a course requirement, a job switch, a research project, or just wanting to finally understand the language your data lives in.

03 / LEARN WITH ME

What I teach

Classes are built around your level and your goal, from a first line of Python to a portfolio-ready ML project.

Python foundations

Syntax, data structures, functions, OOP, file handling and the habits that make code easy to read six months later.

Data science

Pandas, NumPy, exploratory data analysis, statistics, data cleaning and visualisation with Matplotlib and Plotly.

Machine learning

scikit-learn and TensorFlow/Keras: regression, classification, clustering, model evaluation and deep learning basics.

SQL & databases

Writing real queries, joins, aggregation and connecting a database to a Python or Django application.

Projects & portfolios

Turning coursework into a project you can show — structured, documented and pushed to GitHub.

Exam & interview prep

Coursework deadlines, university assignments, and coding-interview practice with real feedback.

Generative AI

Working with LLMs directly: prompting well, the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs, embeddings, and retrieval-augmented generation.

AI agents

Building agents that call tools and APIs — with frameworks like LangChain and LangGraph, from a single tool call to a multi-step workflow.

06 / GOOD QUESTIONS

A little clarity.
Before we begin.

About learning together, the projects, and what to expect.

Ask me something else →
Do I need coding experience to get started?+

No. Python foundations starts with syntax, data structures and functions. If you already code, we can focus on data analysis, machine learning or the specific project you want to build.

How are the classes structured?+

Classes are one-to-one and online. We agree on your starting point, learning goal and schedule, then work through explanations, coding practice and feedback at your pace.

What does a SMART learning plan look like?+

Choose a specific outcome, agree on a measurable checkpoint, scope it to your current level, connect it to your goal, and set a realistic review date together. For example: clean one dataset and explain three charts by an agreed milestone.

Can we work on my own dataset or project?+

Yes. Share your goal and the kind of data or code you are working with. We can plan support around data cleaning, analysis, model evaluation or a documented project you can explain yourself.

Which time zones do you teach in?+

Students join from North America, Europe, the Middle East, Australia, Singapore and other locations. Send your time zone and preferred windows so we can agree on a schedule.

How much do classes cost?+

Fees depend on the subject, class length and scope. Contact me for a quote. The booking arrangement is a 20% advance, with the remaining fee split into three instalments across the agreed course or project.

Are these project previews real outputs?+

Yes. The six image previews are committed output files imported from my public GitHub repositories. Each has an output source and an exact code link. Projects without committed outputs are labeled as source-only.

Can I run the code snippets on their own?+

The snippets are exact excerpts, not standalone programs. Open the linked repository for the full script, required data and setup instructions. Check its license before reusing code.

Do the charts prove a model’s accuracy?+

No. Distributions, correlations and projections show aspects of a dataset or analysis. Model performance needs its own evaluation and validation. This gallery does not claim accuracy scores that are not evidenced here.

What should I send in my first message?+

Tell me what you want to learn or build, your current experience, any deadline and your time zone. You can use WhatsApp or email from the contact section.
